subject: FinHealth Private VPC discovery recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finhealth.com>, Sara Li <sara.li@finhealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: FinHealth Private VPC discovery recap

Tom / Sara — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Regulated data (PCI + SOC2 scope) that cannot egress to public internet or third-party multi-tenant services.
- Existing ML infra is on a private VPC with strict outbound firewall rules; any vendor must support customer-managed keys and audit logs.
- Desire to avoid sending PHI/PII to vendor-managed S3 or analytics without encryption and retention controls.

Current stack and constraints you mentioned:
- Primary environment: AWS account (us-east-1) with private subnets and controlled NAT/egress via firewall appliances.
- Internal inference infra: on-prem inference for some workloads; investigating hybrid approach to reduce ops burden.
- KMS: use of AWS KMS with separate CMKs per environment; key rotation policies enforced by Security.
- Network: no incoming(*) public IPs allowed on sensitive subnets; approved outbound ports: 443 only, and cross-account VPC peering for backend systems.

Success criteria for a pilot:
- Deployment model: Redwood Private (VPC) or on-prem package with no customer data leaving FinHealth-managed network.
- Security: support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and regular access/audit logs (SSE, request tracing).
- Performance: 95th percentile latency < 250ms for typical 512-token requests in the pilot workload.
- Operational: ability for FinHealth SRE to roll back to a pinned model version and run local healthchecks.

Risks / blockers we flagged:
- Air-gapped environments: if you require full air-gap, that adds packaging and validation time (we’ll need to confirm scope).
- Network topology changes: if we must establish private peering, timing depends on your networking team availability.

Action items / next steps:
1) Redwood to provide: SOC2 snapshot & security evidence (attached), high-level network diagram template for your team to annotate (attached).
2) FinHealth to confirm: preferred deployment path (Private VPC vs on-prem), and share a redacted network diagram showing where the inference endpoints would sit.
3) Schedule a technical follow-up with your SRE/networking folks — propose Fri 10/08 or Mon 10/11.
4) Redwood SE (Dylan) to run an internal feasibility check on the CMK/HSM integration and provide a short implementation plan.

Attachments: SOC2-snapshot-2025.pdf (security evidence stub), network-diagram-template.pdf (for FinHealth to fill).

If anything above is incorrect or missing, please flag and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll coordinate schedules for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Li <sara.li@finhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 18:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: FinHealth Private VPC discovery recap

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the call. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The primary path we want to explore is Private VPC deployment (peering or PrivateLink) rather than fully air-gapped at first. Air-gap would be a later option for very sensitive lines of business.
- For KMS: we use AWS KMS now but we have an HSM provider in scope for later; for the pilot we need the vendor integration to support customer-managed CMKs.
- On compliance: we need the vendor to provide SOC2 Type II evidence and a list of subprocessor locations (data residency notes).

Next steps from FinHealth:
- I’ll loop in our SRE lead, Sara (cc’d), to coordinate the network diagram and confirm available dates.
- We prefer the technical deep-dive on Mon 10/11 in the morning PT.

One question: can you include a short note on expected telemetry (what logs / events Redwood will surface in the console) so our auditors can preview?

Appreciate it — Tom
Tom Nguyen
Head of Engineering, FinHealth
tom.nguyen@finhealth.com | (617) 555-2233

Can you please own the following before Mon?
- Dylan: can you draft a one-page implementation note on CMK integration options (KMS vs bring-your-HSM) and list any limitations for the Redwood Private appliance? Also include expected 95p latency estimates for a 512-token gen on g4dn-like infra.
- Aditya: can you pull the telemetry summary (types of events / retention / access logs / request ids) we can share with their auditors and confirm where logs would be stored for Private VPC deployments?

I’ve attached the SOC2 snapshot and the diagram we asked them to annotate. I’ll book the Mon 10/11 09:00 PT slot pending your availability and will include their SRE.
